messages:
aisha_cs: Hey — escalating an on-call ticket from ACME. They say their rerank endpoint returned wildly different scores for the exact same inputs after yesterday's model patch. Customer says production traffic saw order flips and some results that used to be identical now differ by ~0.12 score points. They're blocking a release.

acme_sre: (shared in thread) example payload + before/after scores 
```
// payload.json
{
  \"query\": \"how do I reset my API key\",
  \"candidates\": [\"Resetting an API key\", \"Rotating credentials\", \"Billing FAQ\"]
}
```
Before (model-qa-v1): scores -> [0.87, 0.63, 0.12]
After (model-qa-v2):  scores -> [0.74, 0.79, 0.15]
They said these were deterministic requests, same request IDs but different scores.

aisha_cs: Their usage pattern is large volumes of short queries; they rely on stable ranks for downstream heuristics. They attached a CSV of 1.2k queries where rank order changed. Want us to triage with urgency.

carlos_ml: Thanks — pinging from ML. Do we have the full request/response headers (x-request-id) for two example hits? Also which runner + quant config was used for v2? Might be floating point/quantization drift.

acme_sre: Provided two request ids: rq_34fa and rq_89bc. No other app-side changes. They observed the regression immediately after deploy.

mina_platform: FYI deploy-bot shows a canary rollout for model-qa-v2 at 2025-11-03T17:08Z across eu-west-1. We switched 20% traffic then ramped to 100% at 17:24Z. I have the deploy logs.

deploy-bot: deploy: model-qa-v2 rolled from canary -> prod (20% -> 100%) by mina_platform at 2025-11-03T17:24:31Z. Config: quant=4bit, kernel=fast-attn-v3, batcher=adaptive.

carlos_ml: That quant setting is a red flag. model-qa-v1 was unquantized FP16, right? Quantization to 4-bit can change ranking margins for close candidates. But a 0.12 shift is big for our reranker. Could also be tokenizer differences or a checkpoint variant. Need exact model checksum.

oliver_oncall: I'm seeing errors in rerank-prod around the same window: occasional 500s for requests hitting the v2 pool, plus increased p99 latency from 120ms -> 320ms for rerank. Stacktrace snippets show `kv-cache out-of-sync` warnings around 17:25Z. Not sure if that's related to score variance.

carlos_ml: kv-cache warnings shouldn't change deterministic scoring — they usually affect generation continuity. For rerank (single-pass scoring) the kernel and quantization are more likely. Can we run the same payload against both versions in a hermetic env and compare logits?

mina_platform: I spun up a repro env: `rerank-test-eu` with v1 (fp16) and v2 (4bit) pinned. I ran the two sample requests. Output below.

```
// CURL
curl -X POST https://rerank-test-eu.redwood.local/score \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"how do I reset my API key","candidates":["Resetting an API key","Rotating credentials","Billing FAQ"]}'
```

v1 logits: [2.31, 1.12, -0.85]
v2 logits: [1.92, 2.04, -0.78]

Converted to scores (softmax): v1 -> [0.87,0.63,0.12] ; v2 -> [0.74,0.79,0.15] (matches customer)

mina_platform: raw kernel/quant info: v2 uses `quantize4_dynamic` with per-channel scale, backend `fast-attn-v3`. Model file checksum: sha256: a1b2c3...f9. v1 checksum: sha256: 00aa11...cc.

carlos_ml: Thanks. Hypothesis: quantization introduced asymmetric rounding that disproportionately affects tokens in candidate 2, inflating its score. Two actionable experiments: 1) run v2 with FP16 (no quant) using same checkpoint to see if checkpoint or quant is culprit; 2) run v2 quant but with deterministic higher-precision accumulation for scoring (if runtime supports).

karen_product: Quick note — customers expect score stability for rerank; we should consider a policy: don't change quantization profile for live rerank models without running the golden set. Can we block further auto-rollouts until we have a CI gate?

mina_platform: I paused further rollouts and put rollback on the canary. Rolling back prod to model-qa-v1 now.

deploy-bot: deploy: rollback -> model-qa-v1 initiated by mina_platform at 2025-11-03T18:01:03Z. Traffic 100% -> model-qa-v1.

oliver_oncall: After rollback, customer confirms order reverted for the two samples. System p99 returned to 130ms. I'll keep monitoring for flappers.

acme_sre: Confirmed — their tests show original ranking restored. They asked for a postmortem and mitigations.

carlos_ml: Running experiment 1 now: loading same checkpoint with FP16 runtime. If FP16 reproduces v1 scores then quantization is the root cause. If not, checkpoint drift or tokenizer mapping changed. I'll attach experiment logs when done.

(30m pass)

carlos_ml: Experiment result: same checkpoint + FP16 -> logits match v1 within 0.01. Same checkpoint + quant4 -> matches v2. Conclusion: quantization caused the drift. Details: candidate tokens contain subword pieces where per-channel scale caused slightly different embedding outputs, amplified through MLP and attention -> different logit deltas.

carlos_ml: Fix options: A) revert quant for rerank models (weaker perf trade but stable) B) adopt quant-aware calibration: run golden eval and tune per-channel scales to preserve ranking ordering on a testset C) use hybrid approach: FP16 for rerank, quant for generation models.

karen_product: Recommend immediate policy = block quantization changes for rerank models unless golden-set pass. Also product wants us to notify other customers who might be affected.

mina_platform: I'll add a preflight check in the rollout pipeline that runs a deterministic golden set (1k queries) and verifies top-1 stability threshold (>= 99.5% match) before ramp to 100%. Adding a feature ticket: INF-1943.

aisha_cs: I'll send ACME a summary and ETA. Also adding CS follow-up to offer dedicated capacity or pinned model if they want zero variance.

carlos_ml: Long term ML action: add quant-aware retraining / distillation and a numeric-sensitivity test to the model onboarding checklist. I'll open ML-ops ticket ML-782.

mina_platform: Recorded postmortem notes and timeline. Will assign owners for INF-1943 and coordinate rollout pipeline change with oncall for a staged deploy.

oliver_oncall: Follow-up: I saw a handful of other customers with small score shifts in the monitoring alerts; none were blocking but we should sweep. I've added an alert on score-drift > 0.05 median across golden set.

aisha_cs: Thanks all. Customer is satisfied with rollback + plan. I'll keep thread open until infra+ml tasks are in flight. Action items: 
- mina_platform: add golden-set gate (INF-1943)
- carlos_ml: propose quant calibration or policy (ML-782)
- oliver_oncall: monitor score-drift alert + postmortem writeup
- aisha_cs: customer comms + offer pinned model

deploy-bot: ticket INF-1943 created by mina_platform.

karen_product: Also capturing this as a product risk: scoring determinism for rerank is a product requirement. We'll schedule a short cross-team working session tomorrow.

aisha_cs: Closing note from ACME: they appreciate the quick rollback and asked us to share the golden-set tests once live. Will loop them in after we have a test harness. :thumbsup:
